attrs.label: Why companies bring in an external SEO consultant
attrs.html:
Why companies bring in an external SEO consultant

Most of our consulting clients have capable teams. They bring us in for three reasons.

  1. 01

    Expertise you don’t have in-house

    Your team knows your business and your customers. What it often hasn’t done before is a migration, an international site structure or a deep technical audit. A consultant has done them many times, and brings that experience on day one.

    • Specialists in technical, content, local and international SEO
    • Lessons from many sites, not just yours
    • Your team learns as it works with us

  2. 02

    You can’t wait for the right hire

    Finding a senior SEO takes time: the search, the interviews, the notice period, then months to learn your site. Meanwhile the gap stays open. A consultant can start in a week or two, and help you hire when you’re ready.

    Hiring a senior SEOSearchInterviewsNoticeRamp-upSeveral months

    Bringing in a consultantStart1–2 weeks

  3. 03

    An outside view on big decisions

    Redesigns, migrations and domain mergers are decisions you make once and get wrong expensively. An independent consultant with no stake in the build checks the plan, asks the awkward questions, and spots the risks before launch.

    • No stake in which agency or platform you choose
    • A second opinion your leadership can trust
    • Risks found while they’re still cheap to fix

Moments when an outside view pays for itself

Six situations where companies most often bring us in, and how we help in each.

Website redesign

A redesign is usually led by design and brand. SEO gets checked at the end, if at all, and by then the templates, navigation and copy are signed off. We join early, so the new site keeps what made the old one rank.

The riskNew templates and shorter copy quietly remove the content, headings and internal links that pages ranked for. Traffic falls weeks after launch, when it’s hardest to fix.

What we do

  • Benchmark the pages that bring in traffic and revenue today
  • Review wireframes and designs before they’re signed off
  • Check content, headings and internal links on every key template
  • Crawl the new site on staging and compare it with the live one
  • Watch rankings and traffic page by page for eight weeks after launch

What you getA redesign review with every issue ranked, signed off before launch.

Site migration

Moving to a new platform, CMS or URL structure changes thousands of addresses at once. Every one that isn’t redirected to the right page loses the rankings and links it built up.

The riskMissing or wrong redirects, redirect chains and pages dropped during the move. A badly planned migration can lose a large share of organic traffic for months.

What we do

  • Crawl every live URL, including old ones that still get links
  • Map each old URL to its closest new page
  • Test every redirect on staging before launch
  • Check robots.txt, sitemaps, canonicals and tracking on launch day
  • Fix 404s and redirect problems daily for the first month

What you getA redirect map, a launch checklist and daily checks after go-live.

Merging domains

After an acquisition or a change of strategy, companies often fold several websites into one. Done well, the main site gets stronger. Done badly, pages compete with each other and authority is lost on the way.

The riskDuplicate pages from both sites competing for the same searches, and backlinks pointing at pages that no longer exist.

What we do

  • Audit every site: traffic, rankings, backlinks and content
  • Decide page by page what to keep, merge, redirect or retire
  • Design one structure that fits the whole business
  • Combine overlapping content into the stronger page
  • Track every domain’s traffic until the merge settles

What you getA merge plan your developers and writers can follow, page by page.

Rebrand or new domain

A new name usually means a new domain. Search engines treat it as a new site until the signals from the old one move across, so the move has to be planned, not just switched on.

The riskLost brand searches, links pointing at the old domain, and a long dip while Google learns to trust the new one.

What we do

  • Plan one-to-one redirects from the old domain to the new one
  • Use Search Console’s change of address tool
  • Ask the most valuable linking sites to update their links
  • Keep the old domain registered and redirecting for years
  • Track brand searches for both names after the switch

What you getA domain move plan, with your brand searches carried across.

Expanding to new markets

Launching in a new country or language looks simple: translate the site and publish. But the structure, hreflang and local research decide whether the new version is ever seen.

The riskCopied content, wrong or missing hreflang, and the wrong country version showing in search, or none at all.

What we do

  • Research demand and competitors in each new market
  • Choose the structure: folders, subdomains or separate domains
  • Set up and test hreflang across every version
  • Brief translators on local search terms, not just words
  • Check each market in Search Console after launch

What you getA market entry plan: structure, hreflang and keywords for each country.

A sudden traffic drop

When organic traffic falls fast, the pressure is to change something, anything. A consultant slows that down long enough to find the real cause, then fixes it in the right order.

The riskPanic changes made before the cause is known can turn a short dip into a long one.

What we do

  • Rule out tracking and reporting changes first
  • Check Search Console for indexing problems and manual actions
  • Line the drop up with releases, migrations and Google updates
  • Find which pages, searches and markets lost traffic
  • Fix in order of impact, and confirm the recovery

What you getA clear cause, a fix plan and a recovery you can track.

SEO consulting services for every part of SEO

Bring us in for one area or all of them. In each one, your team does the work and we make sure it’s the right work.

SEO strategy

Most in-house teams don’t lack effort. They lack a clear order of work. We study your market, competitors and data, then write a strategy that says what to do, in what order, and what it should be worth.

What we help with

  • Keyword and competitor research for your market
  • Opportunities ranked by revenue, not search volume
  • A 90-day roadmap with owners and dates
  • Targets your leadership team can sign off
  • A plan sized to your team’s real capacity

Your teamShare data, sign off priorities, do the work

Your consultantResearch, strategy, roadmap and reviews

Common question

How long does an SEO strategy take?

Usually two to four weeks, depending on the size of the site and how much data you can share.

Technical SEO

Technical advice is only useful if your developers can act on it. We write every issue as a ticket, with the cause, the fix and an example, and review the change before it goes live.

What we help with

  • Crawling, indexing and site structure checked
  • Page speed and Core Web Vitals
  • Tickets with code examples for your developers
  • Releases checked on staging before launch
  • Schema and structured data

Your teamBuild and release the fixes

Your consultantFind issues, write tickets, review changes

Common question

Can you work with our developers directly?

Yes. Most clients add us to their ticket system and Slack, so developers can ask questions as they work.

Content and keywords

We decide which pages your site needs, and brief each one so your writers know the search intent, the questions to answer and the pages to link to. Then we review drafts before they’re published.

What we help with

  • Keyword mapping: one clear topic for each page
  • Briefs with intent, headings, questions and links
  • Draft reviews with tracked comments
  • Updates for pages that are losing rankings
  • A content calendar your team can keep to

Your teamWrite and publish

Your consultantPlan, brief and review

Common question

Do you write the content too?

We can. Our writers can take on any pages your team can’t, and every page is written by people.

Local and international

Several branches or several countries add work that’s easy to get wrong: location pages, Google Business Profiles, hreflang and regional sites. We set up the structure and show your team how to run it.

What we help with

  • Location pages that aren’t copies of each other
  • Google Business Profile set-up and reviews
  • Site structure for several countries and languages
  • Hreflang checked across every version
  • Market research before you expand

Your teamRun the profiles and pages

Your consultantStructure, set-up and checks

Common question

Do we need a separate site for each country?

Usually not. Folders on one domain are easier to run and keep your authority in one place.

Redesigns and migrations

Redesigns, new platforms and domain changes are where most sites lose rankings. We plan the redirects, check the new site before launch and watch rankings closely for the weeks after.

What we help with

  • Every old URL mapped to its new page
  • Redirects tested before launch
  • The new site crawled on staging
  • Launch-day and launch-week checks
  • Rankings and traffic tracked page by page

Your teamBuild and launch the new site

Your consultantPlan, check and watch

Common question

When should we bring an SEO consultant into a redesign?

Before the design is signed off. It’s much cheaper to plan the structure than to fix it after launch.

AI search

People now ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Google’s AI Overviews as well as searching. We check where your brand appears in AI answers, what those tools cite, and what to change so they cite you.

What we help with

  • AI answers checked for your main topics
  • Pages and sources that AI tools cite
  • Clear answers and structure on key pages
  • Mentions on the sites AI tools trust
  • Changes tracked month by month

Your teamUpdate pages and earn mentions

Your consultantResearch, priorities and tracking

Common question

Is SEO still worth it with AI search?

Yes. AI tools mostly cite pages that already rank well, so strong SEO is still the way in.

attrs.label: Questions clients bring to our consultants
attrs.html:
Questions clients bring to our consultants

“Every week our clients bring us questions like these. Here are the short versions of our answers. On a call, we go through the detail for your site.”

Sarah Mitchell, Lead SEO consultant

  • Marketing manager · furniture retailer

    Our developer wants to change every URL in the redesign. Should we let them?

    Arjun MehtaTechnical SEO consultant

    Only where the new URL is clearly better. Every change needs a redirect and usually brings a dip for a few weeks. We map every old URL first and keep the ones that already rank.

  • Head of marketing · law firm

    Should we publish 50 blog posts this year, or fix our service pages?

    Elena RossiContent SEO consultant

    Fix the service pages first. They’re the pages that bring in enquiries, and a few strong ones usually beat fifty posts nobody searches for.

  • Founder · software company

    An agency promised us page one in 30 days. Is that realistic?

    Sarah MitchellLead SEO consultant

    No. Nobody controls Google’s rankings. A good consultant gives you a forecast based on your data, and explains what it depends on.

  • eCommerce lead · fashion brand

    Our organic traffic fell 30% last week. What do we check first?

    James WalkereCommerce SEO consultant

    Check tracking first, then Search Console for indexing problems, then whether a release or a Google update lines up with the drop. Most sudden drops have a technical cause.

  • Content lead · travel company

    How many keywords should one page target?

    Elena RossiContent SEO consultant

    One main topic per page, with the close variations that share the same intent. Two pages chasing the same search usually hold each other back.

  • Operations director · clinic group

    Do we need a separate page for every service we offer?

    Daniel CruzInternational SEO consultant

    Yes, if people search for each service on its own. One page per service ranks better and answers each patient’s question directly.

attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What is SEO consulting?
items.answer: SEO consulting is expert advice for businesses that do their SEO in-house. A consultant writes the strategy, sets priorities, and guides and reviews your team’s work.

items.question: What does an SEO consultant do?
items.answer: An SEO consultant reviews your site and market, decides what to work on first, writes tickets and briefs for your team, checks work before it goes live and reports on progress.

items.question: How much do SEO consulting services cost?
items.answer: It depends on the size of your site and how much help your team needs. Every engagement is a fixed price, quoted after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: SEO consultant or SEO agency: which do I need?
items.answer: Choose a consultant if your team can do the work and needs direction. Choose an agency if no one has time for SEO. We offer both, and can mix them.

items.question: How long does SEO consulting take to show results?
items.answer: Technical fixes and page updates often show results within two to three months. Bigger gains usually build over six to twelve months.

items.question: Why hire an external SEO consultant?
items.answer: To bring in expertise your team doesn’t have, without waiting months to hire, and to get an independent view on big decisions such as a redesign, a site migration or merging domains.

items.question: Do you implement the changes yourselves?
items.answer: Your team usually does, with our guidance. If you need hands, our developers and writers can take on any part of the work.

items.question: Can you train our team?
items.answer: Yes. Monthly advisory includes workshops on the topics your team is working on, such as writing pages that rank or checking releases.

items.question: Do you work with teams in other countries?
items.answer: Yes. We work remotely with in-house teams around the world, over video calls, Slack, Teams and email.
